_doc: The brand palette, in one place. Everything else reads this file.
scripts/apply-brand-tokens.py rewrites the :root block in assets/css/style.css from
here, so a future rebrand is an edit to this file and one run, not a hunt through
2,500 CSS lines, 13 guide diagrams and three head-tag generators.
Every value below was measured, not chosen by eye. 'ratio_white' is the contrast
against #ffffff; anything a label sits on or is painted in must reach 4.5,
verify.py re-checks these, so a careless edit here fails the gate rather than
shipping a button nobody can read.

--brand.role: THE MARK'S OWN TEAL, unchanged from pin-100.svg

--brand-deep.role: link ink and CTA gradient start

--gold.role: the mark's gold. DECORATION ONLY: never a label, never behind white text

--gold-deep.role: gold that has to carry text

--sky.role: the info accent; lifts on dark

--indigo.role: the second accent; lifts on dark

--tint-bg.role: every informational chip, badge and quiet panel

--line.role: the rule above a page's byline

--nav-glass.role: the sticky nav's translucent glass; derived from --bg per mode so the bar can never stay light in night mode

unchanged: the status family (--danger, --warn) - teal is 128 points off red, so a failure still cannot be mistaken for brand
--maps-red, the Google Maps pin used once on the directory row

--text-inv.role: ink that sits ON the brand; the button label

--mark.role: mile markers, centreline and signage: brand ink on the hero map

--ink.role: the hero map's deep brand ink

--ocean.role: the hero map's mid brand wash

--route-body.role: the driving route's ribbon: the signature teal, and the one colour on the map that moves

_superseded_note: The blue ladder and its tint family, retired 2026-11-05. Listed so the checker can refuse them if a rebrand forgets a token; a stale value in the layer is exactly how #mark stayed blue.
_dark_doc: Day/night. Every colour token above carries a 'dark' value; the generator emits a
second block after the light one, and assets/js/site.js decides which is in play
by putting data-mode on the root. One file, one run, both themes.
The MAP group is deliberately absent: a highway map is not a light/dark surface.
Recolouring asphalt, signage and the route ribbon for dark would break the map's
own legibility (white sign text on a lifted sign, a route ribbon that has to stay
the signature teal). The map is identical in both modes by decision, not by
oversight. --map-fade and --route-fade are fractions, not colours, so they have
no dark value for the same reason --bg does not have two.
Contrast, measured against the dark page #0f172a:
white on the dark --brand #14b8a6 does NOT pass, which is why --text-inv is
near-black in dark mode: the button label flips with the fill it sits on.

--danger.role: the ink and edge of a failed verdict (lint: on dark it must LIFT, not darken)

--danger-soft.role: the rose used for error borders and dots

--maps-red.role: the map marker red: decorative, reads on both, so it does NOT flip

--warn.role: caution ink (lint: dark amber on a dark wash, the light value would vanish)
